JHX Hoops is one win away from TBT Championship game

Shay Wildeboor@JayhawkSlant
07/28/26
Keep Watching
2027 Bracketology: ESPN updates mid-August NCAA Tournament projections
Watch More
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:41
Instaread

Frank Mason did it again for JHX Hoops. Leading AfterShocks, 61-59, in the semifinal round of TBT inside Charles Koch Arena, Mason drilled a three to win the game and, more importantly, move KU’s alumni team just one game away from competing for the $2 million prize.

It’s certainly been a memorable ride for Mason and his JHX Hoops teammates. For Mason, it all started on Wednesday night when his driving layup inside Lee Area forced a third and decisive game against Purple Reign.

In that final game, Mason, as he’d done two nights earlier, scored on a drive to the basket, which eliminated Purple Reign from TBT.

Playing AfterShocks inside Charles Koch Arena in Wichita, Kansas, with the winner advancing to face La Familia (Kentucky) in Lexington, Kentucky, on Wednesday night, both JHX Hoops and AfterShocks found themselves shorthanded after a scuffle broke out under the basket shortly before halftime.

After a lengthy delay, JHX Hoops was left with just six players — Frank Mason, Jacob Hanna, Carlton Bragg, Zeke Mayo, Billy Preston, and Andrew Orr.

The Wichita State alumni team was equally shorthanded, as Markis McDuffie, Corey Washington, Marcus Keene, Trey Wade, Conner Frankamp, and Marcus Santos-Silva were left standing following the scuffle.

Down by two points, 27-25 at the half, JHX Hoops took its first lead of the third quarter, 28-27, on a layup by Zeke Mayo. However, it didn’t take long for AfterShocks to respond and, with 4:33 left in the third quarter, JHX Hoops trailed 36-31.

Up by four points, 48-44, at the start of the fourth quarter, JHX Hoops found itself trading baskets with AfterShocks for the first four minutes of the quarter.

When the game was stopped for the start of the Elam Ending, JHX Hoops found itself up by one point, 56-55. Mayo put JHX Hoops up by three points following a turnover by Marcus Keene. After a series of empty possessions by both teams, Mason hit back-to-back threes to send JHX Hoops on to Lexington, Kentucky, to face La Familia on Wednesday night.

The winner of JHX Hoops and La Familia will be crowned the Alumni Champion of TBT. The winner will also face the Non-Alumni Champion, with the winning team walking away with the $2 million prize.

In defeating AfterShocks, Mayo led the way with 25 points. He was 10-of-20 from the field, 3-of-9 from behind the arc, and 2-of-4 from the free-throw line.

Jacob Hanna added 15 points on 5-of-13 shooting from the field and 5-of-6 from the free-throw line.

Mason, who hit the game-winner, finished with 13 points on 5-of-21 shooting from the field, including 3-of-8 from behind the arc.

2027 Bracketology: Latest way-too-early NCAA Tournament projections after 5-for-5 decisions

James Fletcher III@jdfletch3

National Reporter

41m
Reporting for

The college basketball offseason is typically settled at the point, but the international market and a new batch of eligible players have added intrigue in August. The NCAA’s five-for-five rule has led to a long list of legal cases involving last year’s senior class, ready to return for another season.

The NCAA Tournament field is officially moving from 68 teams to 76 this season, leaving more room for bubble teams to enter the mix after expansion. After the NBA Draft withdrawal decisions last month, the college basketball landscape continues to become more clear.

The NCAA uses the NET Rankings – an analytic algorithm that ranks every team in college basketball by splitting wins and losses into four categories (known as quadrants) – to help the selection committee build the new 76-team bracket in March. Bracketology aims to predict how the selection committee will seed each team based on the results to this point in the season while accounting for other factors that impact the final bracket.

With the new additions to several rosters changing how offseason rankings look, there is plenty still moving before November’s season tip-off. Using that information, here is another way-too-early look at the 2027 Bracketology field from On3 based on those changes.

Bracketology

Projected 1-line: Florida, Duke, UConn, Michigan State
Last four byes: Clemson, Wisconsin, Georgia, VCU
Last four in: Oklahoma State, Arizona State, Stanford, Oregon
First four out: Utah, Xavier, Creighton, Ole Miss

1-seed Florida

Florida has plenty of talent set to return for the 2026-27 season, bringing back valuable pieces to the backcourt and frontcourt. The latest news that Thomas Haugh will return for another season alongside Alex Condon is enough to push them into the top spot, with another international reinforcement coming.

2-seed Michigan

Michigan looks likely to stay near the top of college basketball next season, with key pieces currently projected to return, along with big additions. The Wolverines have once again invested big in the frontcourt across recruiting and the transfer portal but lose Dusty May with assistant Mike Boynton taking over.

West (Los Angeles)

Louisville
1 Michigan State (Big Ten) vs. 16 Merrimack/Long Island
8 Missouri vs. 9 St. Louis (A10)
Minneapolis

3 Arkansas vs. 14 Akron (MAC)
Fort Worth

2 Houston vs. 15 Arkansas State/Austin Peay

1-seed Michigan State

Michigan State will bring back plenty of talent to the backcourt and the wings next season, although the frontcourt will see big turnover. The incoming recruiting class will help fill gaps, but it will be a position to watch in the transfer portal.

2-seed Houston

Houston remains a top team year after year, bringing in another talented recruiting class to complement a returning group. The Cougars also did early work in the transfer portal, quickly building out a solid rotation for next season.

Charlotte

Fort Worth

1-seed Duke

Duke puts together another top-end recruiting class with multiple top prospects, all slotting in different areas of the court. The Blue Devils have confirmed the return of multiple starters while adding highly-rated transfers.

2-seed Texas

Texas has built up one of the best transfer portal classes in college basketball, ready to compete at the top of the SEC in Year Two under Sean Miller. The Longhorns also hit the recruiting trail for a balance of potential and production across the roster.

South (San Antonio)

Pittsburgh

8 Iowa vs. 9 BYU

2 Illinois vs. 15 Wright State (Horizon)

1-seed UConn

UConn could get back the core of a talented backcourt next season, also hitting the recruiting trail for a talented group of players. The addition of Najai Hines was backed up by the return of star freshman Braylon Mullins, while offseason surgery for Solo Ball will hurt.

2-seed Illinois

Illinois can bring back a good chunk of its talent next season, setting it up to bring in a talented freshman class ready to run the backcourt. The addition of Stefan Vaaks through the transfer portal will help ease that transition as they build on last season.
